Consumer Non-Cyclicals: Consumer Non-Cyclicals posted an average annual earnings growth of 34.91% over the past year, placing the sector tenth out of fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Revenue grew at a more modest 10.44% average, earning the sector the sixth spot in revenue growth rankings. [#VC2.SI]Olam Group Ltd[\#VC2.SI] delivered the strongest earnings acceleration within the group, while [#EB5.SI]First Resources Ltd[\#EB5.SI] recorded the highest revenue increase. The sector’s performance is reinforced by Singapore’s emphasis on food security, which drives investment in agribusiness and downstream processing, as well as by stable household spending on essential goods that is less sensitive to economic cycles. Additionally, regulatory incentives for local sourcing of consumer staples help sustain demand for companies operating in this space.
Consumer Cyclicals: Despite a decline in earnings, the Consumer Cyclicals sector posted solid revenue expansion, with an average annual earnings growth of -6.91% and an average annual revenue growth of 14.44% over the past year. The sector ranks 14th out of 15 for earnings growth, highlighting the pressure on profit margins, while it ranks 3rd for revenue growth, indicating strong top‑line performance. [#51O.SI]MSM International Ltd[\#51O.SI] delivered the highest yearly earnings growth in the group, and [#5OX.SI]Mary Chia Holdings Ltd[\#5OX.SI] achieved the highest yearly revenue growth. Growth in Singapore’s consumer cyclicals is uniquely shaped by the sector’s reliance on tourism inflows, which boost retail and hospitality sales, and by seasonal spending spikes around festivals such as Chinese New Year. Additionally, government measures that affect car ownership costs and housing affordability influence discretionary spending patterns, further differentiating the sector’s performance from other industries.
Transportation & Logistics: The Transportation & Logistics sector recorded an average annual earnings growth of 1.75% and a slightly stronger average annual revenue growth of 2.71% over the past year. This places the sector 13th out of 15 in earnings growth and 12th out of 15 in revenue growth, indicating modest performance relative to other SGX sectors. Within the sector, [#FQ7.SI]Salt Investments Ltd[\#FQ7.SI] delivered the highest yearly earnings growth, while [#R14.SI]Eneco Energy Ltd[\#R14.SI] achieved the top revenue growth. Growth in Singapore’s logistics landscape is shaped by the nation’s continued expansion of port infrastructure, which improves cargo handling capacity and attracts more trans‑shipment activity. Additionally, the government’s emphasis on digitalising freight operations and tightening emissions standards for commercial vehicles creates both opportunities and cost pressures unique to this sector.
Healthcare: Healthcare sector posted an average annual earnings growth of 24.57% while revenue grew 4.64% over the past year. This earnings expansion placed the sector 11th out of 15 sectors, and the revenue increase ranked it 9th out of 15. The strongest earnings performance came from [#FHH.SI]FHH[\#FHH.SI], which recorded the highest yearly earnings growth within the sector, whereas [#8YY.SI]Embracing Future Holdings Ltd[\#8YY.SI] led the sector in revenue growth. In Singapore, the sector benefits from an increasingly aging population that raises demand for medical services and chronic‑disease management, as well as sustained government investment in public health infrastructure. At the same time, tighter regulatory scrutiny on drug approvals and the need to comply with local healthcare standards create additional operational considerations unique to the market.
Properties & Real Estate: Properties & Real Estate posted an average annual earnings growth of 87.6%, placing it third among fifteen SGX sectors for earnings expansion. Revenue in the same period rose by 13.08% on average, earning the sector the fourth best rank for revenue growth. The strongest drivers were seen at [#5IC.SI][#5IC.SI]SING Holdings Ltd[\#5IC.SI][\#5IC.SI], which recorded the highest yearly earnings growth and also led the sector in revenue growth. Growth was further supported by Singapore’s constrained land availability, which pushes up property values, and by recent government cooling measures that have reshaped demand toward higher-quality developments. Additionally, rising construction material costs and tighter financing criteria for developers have uniquely shaped the sector’s performance.
Energy: The Energy sector posted an impressive average annual earnings growth of 45.69% over the past year, while its average annual revenue growth reached 21.15%. Among fifteen SGX sectors, it ranks eighth for earnings growth and leads the pack at first place for revenue growth. [#JFQ.SI]JFQ[\#JFQ.SI] recorded the strongest yearly earnings expansion within the sector, and [#TPED.SI]PTT Exploration Production PCL DRC[\#TPED.SI] delivered the highest yearly revenue increase. Growth has been buoyed by Singapore’s strategic position as a regional hub for oil and gas trading, coupled with recent policy incentives that encourage investment in cleaner energy infrastructure, which have uniquely supported the sector’s performance. These sector‑specific dynamics, together with robust demand for power generation across Southeast Asia, have reinforced the strong financial momentum.
Utilities: Despite a robust earnings expansion of 48.42% on average, the Utilities sector recorded a contraction in revenue of 5.18% over the past year. The sector ranks sixth among fifteen sectors for earnings growth, but falls to the bottom position for revenue growth. [#5GD.SI]Sunpower Group Ltd[\#5GD.SI] delivered the strongest earnings acceleration within the group, while [#BEH.SI]China International Holdings Ltd[\#BEH.SI] achieved the highest revenue increase despite the overall decline. Growth in earnings is partly driven by Singapore’s ongoing grid modernization program and higher tariffs approved for renewable electricity, which benefit companies with solar and wind assets. Conversely, revenue pressure stems from tighter water pricing regulations and the gradual shift toward energy‑efficiency measures that reduce consumption volumes. These Singapore‑specific policy and infrastructure dynamics shape the divergent performance observed in the Utilities sector.
Consumer Defensive: The Consumer Defensive sector posted an impressive average annual earnings growth of 53.45% over the past year, placing it fifth among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Revenue in the sector rose by 10.83% on average, also earning a fifth‑place ranking for revenue growth. [#CNE.SI]MindChamps PreSchool Ltd[\#CNE.SI] led the sector in earnings acceleration, while [#5EG.SI]Zhongxin Fruit and Juice Ltd[\#5EG.SI] delivered the strongest revenue increase. Growth has been reinforced by Singapore’s focus on food safety standards, which boosts demand for locally produced fruit and juice, and by government support for early‑childhood education that benefits providers such as [#CNE.SI]MindChamps PreSchool Ltd[\#CNE.SI]. These sector‑specific dynamics have helped sustain the strong performance.
Financial Services: The Financial Services sector posted an average annual earnings growth of 8.14% and an average annual revenue growth of 8.23% over the past year. This earnings growth placed the sector 12th out of 15 sectors, while its revenue growth ranked it 8th, highlighting a stronger performance on the top line than on profitability. [#I49.SI]IFS Capital Ltd[\#I49.SI] delivered the highest yearly earnings growth within the sector, and [#K6S.SI]Prudential PLC[\#K6S.SI] recorded the strongest revenue growth. Growth was further supported by Singapore's progressive regulatory framework that encourages fintech innovation and by rising demand for wealth management services as the population ages, both of which uniquely boost financial firms in the local market.
Communication Services: Despite a modest revenue increase of about 3.01%, the Communication Services sector recorded a sharp decline in earnings, with an average annual earnings change of -108.57%. This places the sector at the bottom of the earnings growth ranking, 15th out of 15, while its revenue growth rank is 11th among the 15 sectors. [#9VW.SI][#9VW.SI]Spackman Entertainment Group Ltd[\#9VW.SI][\#9VW.SI] led the sector on both fronts, delivering the highest yearly earnings growth and the strongest revenue expansion. In Singapore, the sector’s performance is shaped by the recent tightening of broadcast licensing rules and higher spectrum fees, which pressure profit margins even as advertising spend slowly recovers. Additionally, the shift toward high-speed mobile data services creates investment demand that boosts top-line revenue but does not immediately translate into earnings. Consequently, the sector shows a divergence between modest top-line growth and severe earnings contraction.
Basic Materials: The Basic Materials sector posted an extraordinary average annual earnings growth of 969.42%, placing it first among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Its average annual revenue grew by 8.66%, which ranks the sector seventh in revenue growth across the same peer group. [#KUO.SI]International Cement Group Ltd[\#KUO.SI] delivered the highest yearly earnings growth within the sector, while [#C8R.SI]Jiutian Chemical Group Ltd[\#C8R.SI] led in revenue growth. In Singapore, the sector’s performance is uniquely shaped by the country’s limited domestic mineral reserves, which drives reliance on imported raw materials and amplifies the impact of global commodity price movements. Additionally, sustained government investment in infrastructure and large‑scale construction projects fuels demand for cement and chemicals, further influencing earnings and revenue trends.
Infrastructures: The Infrastructures sector posted an average annual earnings growth of about 336.27%, placing it second among fifteen SGX sectors for earnings expansion, while its average annual revenue growth was modest at roughly 1.84%, ranking fourteenth for revenue increase. [#Z74.SI]Singapore Telecommunications Ltd[\#Z74.SI] delivered the strongest earnings surge within the sector, and [#S59.SI]SIA Engineering Co Ltd[\#S59.SI] recorded the highest revenue growth. The sector’s earnings acceleration is driven by Singapore’s ongoing rollout of next‑generation broadband networks and the expansion of data centre capacity, which create substantial upside for telecom operators. At the same time, revenue growth remains limited by the capital‑intensive nature of infrastructure projects and the regulatory pacing of large‑scale construction permits. Additionally, the island’s status as a regional aviation hub fuels demand for engineering services, supporting [#S59.SI]SIA Engineering Co Ltd[\#S59.SI]’s performance, while government initiatives on smart city and climate‑resilient infrastructure shape the sector’s outlook.
REIT: The REIT sector posted an average annual earnings growth of 37.31% over the past year, placing it ninth among fifteen sectors. Its average annual revenue grew 4.36%, ranking it tenth in revenue growth. [#M1GU.SI]Alpha Integrated REIT[\#M1GU.SI] led the sector in earnings growth, while [#DCRU.SI]Digital Core REIT[\#DCRU.SI] delivered the strongest revenue expansion. Growth in Singapore’s REIT market is uniquely influenced by the island’s limited land supply, the government’s focus on developing high‑quality commercial and logistics properties, and the sector’s sensitivity to interest‑rate movements that affect dividend yields and investor demand.
Industrials: The Industrials sector posted an impressive average annual earnings growth of 59.82% over the past year. This placed the sector fourth among fifteen sectors in earnings growth. By contrast, average annual revenue grew only 2.47%, ranking it thirteenth for revenue growth. Within the sector, [#5OC.SI]Koyo International Ltd[\#5OC.SI] delivered the strongest earnings expansion, while [#Y06.SI]Green Build Technology Ltd[\#Y06.SI] led revenue growth. The sector’s performance is shaped by Singapore’s ongoing expansion of its port facilities and increased government investment in infrastructure projects, which boost demand for industrial equipment and services. At the same time, tighter land availability and higher construction costs temper revenue growth, contributing to the modest increase.
Technology: Singapore’s Technology sector posted an impressive average annual earnings growth of about 46.45% over the past year, while average annual revenue grew 15.2%. This earnings pace placed the sector seventh among fifteen sectors, whereas its revenue expansion ranked second, highlighting a stronger top‑line momentum relative to peers. The leading driver of earnings growth was [#BLU.SI]GRP Ltd[\#BLU.SI], which recorded the highest yearly increase in profit within the sector, and [#9MT.SI]MetaOptics Ltd[\#9MT.SI] delivered the strongest revenue surge. Growth was further supported by Singapore’s aggressive smart‑nation initiatives that accelerate adoption of enterprise cloud services and the expansion of local data‑centre capacity, both of which create a fertile environment for technology firms. In addition, the country’s high broadband penetration and government incentives for research and development help sustain the sector’s rapid expansion.
